description: Part XVIII of the Indian Constitution deals with Emergency Provisions, along with other miscellaneous subjects like Constitutional Amendments and Official Languages. These provisions are crucial to safeguard the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of the country during crises.

sections.title: National Emergency
sections.description: Provisions related to the emergency declared by the President for the security of the country during war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

key_concepts.explanation: Contained in Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) of the Constitution. During an emergency, the federal structure converts into a unitary one. This feature is inspired by the Weimar Constitution of Germany.

historical_events.significance: Imposed due to the Indo-China War.
Imposed by the Indira Gandhi government on the controversial grounds of 'Internal Disturbance'.

polity_articles.details: Grounds: War, External Aggression, or Armed Rebellion. The 44th Amendment Act replaced the term 'Internal Disturbance' with 'Armed Rebellion'.

sections.title: President's Rule (State Emergency)
sections.description: The takeover of the state government by the Center in the event of the failure of constitutional machinery in the states.

polity_articles.provision: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States.
polity_articles.details: Popularly known as President's Rule or State Emergency. It is generally imposed on the receipt of a report from the Governor of the state.

polity_articles.provision: Effect of failure to comply with directions given by the Union.
polity_articles.details: If a state fails to comply with the directions given by the Center, it shall be lawful for the President to hold that a situation has arisen where the state government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

important_facts.fact: President's Rule was imposed for the first time in India in the state of Punjab in 1951.
President's Rule can be extended for 6 months at a time with parliamentary approval, up to a maximum duration of 3 years.

sections.title: Financial Emergency and Impact on Fundamental Rights
sections.description: Rules associated with emergencies during financial instability and the suspension of citizens' rights during emergency periods.

polity_articles.details: Declared if the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. This provision is inspired by the Constitution of the USA.

polity_articles.provision: Suspension of provisions of Article 19 during emergencies.
polity_articles.details: The 6 fundamental rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended as soon as a National Emergency is declared (only on the grounds of war or external aggression).

polity_articles.provision: Suspension of the enforcement of fundamental rights during emergencies.
polity_articles.details: The President is authorized to suspend by order the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21).

important_facts.fact: A Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been imposed in India to date.

sections.title: Amendment of the Constitution
sections.description: The power and procedure of the Parliament to amend the Constitution as laid down in Part XX.

key_concepts.explanation: In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament can amend the Constitution under Article 368, but it cannot destroy or alter its 'Basic Structure'.

polity_articles.provision: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor.
polity_articles.details: Provides for two types of amendments: by a Special Majority of Parliament, and by a Special Majority of Parliament along with the ratification by half of the State Legislatures.

key_associations.item: Procedure for Amendment of the Constitution
key_associations.extra_info: The process of amending the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the South African Constitution.

sections.title: Official Language and Special Provisions
sections.description: Important articles from Part XVII (Official Language) and Part XXI (Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions).

polity_articles.details: States that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script.

polity_articles.provision: Directive for development of the Hindi language.
polity_articles.details: It shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language, to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India.

polity_articles.provision: Special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
polity_articles.details: Provides for the establishment of separate development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra, etc.

important_facts.fact: Article 370, which previously granted special autonomous status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir, was essentially abrogated in August 2019.
